narrative: 有人在看。反打镜头（Reverse Angle）拍的是占据视线另一端的那个人或那件事物。
在餐馆里，它是对面的卡座。在枪战中，它是对方的枪套。
景别和高度的匹配能让这次剪辑不显得像换了一场戏。反打镜头可以是干净的单人镜头（Single），也可以是过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）；这个名称说的是轴线关系，而不是前景的肩膀。
不给出反打镜头是另一种剪辑选择：一个看的动作、一个反应，却没有回应的画面。《女巫布莱尔》（The Blair Witch Project）和《罗斯玛丽的婴儿》（Rosemary's Baby）就活在这种拒绝给出反打的状态里。
反打镜头本身指的是那个"给出回应"的机位，而不是拒绝给出回应。
how: 遵守180度轴线。把摄影机移到轴线的对面一侧，但仍留在同一条线的同一侧，并让镜头高度匹配新的拍摄对象（坐姿还是站姿、成人还是孩子）。
景别要与上一个镜头匹配，除非这次剪辑本就是要制造冲击感。视线必须穿越同一片空气交汇。
提示词：reverse angle, opposing view of the dialogue or standoff, 180-line respected, geography flipping.
when: 用它来完成轴线关系：展示他们看的到底是谁。具体场景：在隔桌一瞥之后，切到另一个人景别相匹配的单人镜头，视线方向相反。
如果这场戏的力量恰恰来自于不揭示被看之物，就不要给出反打镜头。
vs: 过肩镜头（Over-the-Shoulder Coverage）是常被用作反打的一种构图，带有近处的肩膀；反打镜头也可以是干净的单人镜头（Single）。主观镜头（Point of View）呈现的是他们所看到的东西，未必是一张脸。
平视（Eye Level）可以在两侧保持一致，但反打说的是相对的机位，而不是高度。侧面镜头（Profile）的双人镜头也可以反打成相对的两个侧面镜头。
examples_film: 《盗火线》（Heat）的餐馆戏在两个四分之三侧面（Three-Quarter Angle）单人镜头上保持了清晰的相对方向。《黄金三镖客》（The Good, the Bad and the Ugly）用同一条轴线上的一系列相互回应的视角，搭建出墓地对峙场面。
《闪灵》（The Shining）红色浴室里的对话，用了令人不安的相对空间视角。《邻居们》（Neighbors, 1920）则是反打镜头间保持方位一致的一个早期范例。
mistakes: 最容易混淆的错误对象是越轴或无故改变景别的新机位。辨别标志：两张脸都望向画面右侧，或用一个全景来回应一个紧特写。
修正方法：视线方向相对，高度和景别匹配，遵守180度轴线。另一种容易混淆的情况是主观镜头（Point of View）：他们注视的一扇空荡的门是主观镜头，而不是对另一个人的反打。

faq.q: 电影中的反打镜头是什么？
faq.a: 反打镜头从相对的一侧展示同样的空间关系。它在遵守180度轴线的前提下，完成一次注视或一场对话的轴线关系。

faq.q: 反打镜头 vs 过肩镜头
faq.a: 反打说的是轴线上相对的那个机位。过肩镜头是一种常被用作反打的构图，前景带有一侧肩膀。反打镜头也可以是干净的单人镜头。

faq.q: 什么时候该用反打镜头？
faq.a: 当观众必须看到一次注视、一场对话或一次对峙的另一端时使用。当这场戏的重点就是不揭示被看之物时，不要用它。

faq.q: 如何为AI图像或视频撰写反打镜头的提示词？
faq.a: 写法：Reverse angle on [Subject], opposing view of the dialogue or standoff, 180-line respected, matching size, eyeline opposite the first shot. 并注明应该翻转的空间方位关系。

narrative: Someone looks. The reverse is who or what occupies the other pole.
In a diner, it is the other booth. In a gunfight, it is the other holster.
Matching size and height keeps the cut from feeling like a new scene. The reverse can be a clean Single or an Over-the-Shoulder Coverage; the name is the axis, not the foreground shoulder.
Withholding the reverse is a different editorial choice: a look, a reaction, and no answering view. The Blair Witch Project and Rosemary's Baby live on that denial.
The reverse-angle shot itself is the answering camera, not the refusal of it.
how: Hold the 180-line. Move the camera to the opposite side of the axis, still on the same side of the line, and match lens height to the new subject (sit versus stand, adult versus child).
Match shot size to the outgoing picture unless the cut is meant to punch. Eyelines must cross the same empty air.
Prompt: reverse angle, opposing view of the dialogue or standoff, 180-line respected, geography flipping.
when: Use it to complete the axis: show who they were looking at. Concrete beat: after a look across a table, the matching-size single of the other person, eyeline opposing.
Do not fire the reverse when the scene's power is the withheld object of the look.
vs: Over-the-Shoulder Coverage is a composition often used as the reverse, with a near shoulder; a reverse can also be a clean Single. Point of View shows what they see, which may not be a face.
Eye Level may match on both sides, but the reverse is the opposing camera, not a height. Profile two-shots can reverse into opposing profiles.
examples_film: Heat 's diner keeps clear opposing screen directions on two three-quarter singles. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly builds the cemetery standoff from answering views along one axis.
The Shining 's red-bathroom talk uses startling opposing spatial views. Neighbors (1920) is an early lesson in preserving orientation across reverses.
mistakes: The usual wrong cousin is a new setup that crosses the line or changes size for no reason. Tell: both faces look camera-right, or a wide answering a choker.
Fix: opposing eyelines, matched height and size, 180-line held. The other mix-up is Point of View: an empty doorway they were watching is a POV, not a reverse on the other person.

faq.q: What is a reverse angle in film?
faq.a: A reverse angle shows the same spatial relationship from the opposing side. It completes a look or a dialogue axis while keeping the 180-degree line.
A reverse is the opposing camera on the axis. Over-the-shoulder is a framing that often serves as that reverse, with a near shoulder in the foreground. The reverse can also be a clean single.

faq.q: When should I use a reverse angle?
faq.a: Use it when the audience must see the other pole of a look, a talk, or a standoff. Do not use it when withholding the object of the look is the point.

faq.q: How do I prompt a reverse angle for AI image or video?
faq.a: Write: Reverse angle on [Subject], opposing view of the dialogue or standoff, 180-line respected, matching size, eyeline opposite the first shot. Name the geography that should flip.
